card.name: Linking words before serious outcome terms
card.fires_on: Small linking words (and, be, of, in, most) and 'subjects/patients' right before a serious outcome or harm term such as irreversible reactions, event, blindness, or vision loss. Seen in boxed warnings, trial tables and eye-disease text.

modes.label: Linking word before harm
modes.description: A short linking word sits just before a word for a severe or lasting adverse effect.
modes.example: have been associated with disabling<< and>> potentially irreversible serious adverse reactions that have occurred

modes.label: Count of subjects with event
modes.description: The noun after 'Number of' in trial-table footnotes, just before 'with event'.
modes.example: c Number of<< subjects>> with event that occurred within 6 months

modes.label: Eye-disease outcomes
modes.description: A linking word in eye-condition text, just before vision-loss terms.
modes.example: the angle-closure glaucoma may result<< in>> permanent visual field loss

card.writes: It lowers the odds of death words and slightly raises career-related words, so it steers away from naming death as the outcome.
card.plain: It fires on the small word just before a serious harm or outcome is named, like vision loss or lasting reactions.
